entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: "“President Rayne, I am here because..."
entries.dialogueText: “President Rayne, I am here because we have a great opportunity on our hands. A business arrangement that will benefit Gasom and Sordland alike.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“And serve you did. Sordland would..."
entries.dialogueText: “And serve you did. Sordland would be much worse off without you.”

entries.dialogueText: "I put so many years of my life into this corporation. And then I left it all behind and devoted myself to serving the people of Sordland."

entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: "“My Gasom is not nearly as bad off..."
entries.dialogueText: “My Gasom is not nearly as bad off as the Sordish government was. But a shake-up is needed nonetheless.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“The latest figures show that Gasom..."
entries.dialogueText: “The latest figures show that Gasom will have to either decrease staff and operations by 40 percent in one year or take on a crushing amount of debt.”

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: "“I appreciate you coming through, G..."
entries.dialogueText: “I appreciate you coming through, Gus. Getting Rizia interested in another investment is a major feat.”

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: "“But I'm concerned about the future..."
entries.dialogueText: “But I'm concerned about the future of what I have built up."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""But let's shift our focus to Gasom.""
entries.dialogueText: "But let's shift our focus to Gasom."

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“This is why we have decided to rea..."
entries.dialogueText: “This is why we have decided to reach out to foreign investors."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: "“We've got an amazing opportunity h..."
entries.dialogueText: “We've got an amazing opportunity here. The demand for gas is steadily increasing from both international partners and the Sordish state. All we have to do is ensure a consistent supply."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""I've had some time to think since..."
entries.dialogueText: "I've had some time to think since leaving office. And to me, all of life's complexities can be distilled into two elements. Reputation and legacy."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: "“With the right amount of investmen..."
entries.dialogueText: “With the right amount of investment, we can expand resource extraction, effectively fulfill rising demand and ensure long-term stability and profitability.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I cannot help but empathize with i..."
entries.dialogueText: "I cannot help but empathize with individuals who invest their utmost dedication and passion into their work."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: "“Not the right choice of words. Thi..."
entries.dialogueText: “Not the right choice of words. This is not a bailout, but a strategic long-term cooperation.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“The fact that a leading privatizer..."
entries.dialogueText: “The fact that a leading privatizer is coming to the state to bail out his corporation is hysterical.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“You do know that Rizia can't inves..."
entries.dialogueText: “You do know that Rizia can't invest more than 20 percent unless the government permits the transaction which can take a long time.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Gasom is a private corporation. Wh..."
entries.dialogueText: “Gasom is a private corporation. What does Sordland have to do with your business?”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“If your analysis is correct, any i..."
entries.dialogueText: “If your analysis is correct, any investment would also make returns and secure further gas.”

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: "“I ventured to Xina, immersing myse..."
entries.dialogueText: “I ventured to Xina, immersing myself in its vibrant culture, then traversed the captivating landscapes of the Anrakan archipelago, and finally reunited with old acquaintances in Kyow.”

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: "“And now that you're in office, you..."
entries.dialogueText: “And now that you're in office, you seem to be turning your back on your ideals entirely. Is power getting to you?”

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: "“I always spoke highly of you, in f..."
entries.dialogueText: “I always spoke highly of you, in fact. The youngest MP, a prodigy, I said. Even though I knew we could be rivals one day.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""It's too early to tell whether the..."
entries.dialogueText: "It's too early to tell whether the Alphonso era was good for Sordland. It'll be a subject of debate among future historians."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""The deviation from our planned eco..."
entries.dialogueText: "The deviation from our planned economic strategy didn't bode well for the nation."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""Gasom still operates, yes. 'Thrive..."
entries.dialogueText: "Gasom still operates, yes. 'Thrives' is perhaps an exaggeration."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""That is much appreciated. I am wel..."
entries.dialogueText: "That is much appreciated. I am well aware of the challenges you yourself have faced. I commend you for navigating those obstacles without causing harm to others."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""That's why Mr. Manger and I have b..."
entries.dialogueText: "That's why Mr. Manger and I have been diligently exploring alternative solutions."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""If Soll had continued, we would ha..."
entries.dialogueText: "If Soll had continued, we would have faced a severe economic downturn as well. The fabric of the country was being torn apart by corruption, greed and autocratic tendencies."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""We're not here to talk about my pr..."
entries.dialogueText: "We're not here to talk about my presidential successes or failures, Mr. Rayne. But I will say this."

entries.title: Narrator: "The sound of sirens briefly distrac..."
entries.dialogueText: The sound of sirens briefly distracted us. Through the window, we saw police cars driving down the street adjacent to the Gasom zone.

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: "“I will remind you that I was never..."
entries.dialogueText: “I will remind you that I was never against the complete removal of the Energy Protection Act of 1932.”

entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""Despite criticism from the Nature..."
entries.dialogueText: "Despite criticism from the Nature Preservation Foundation, I fulfilled most of the gas needs of Sordland and increased our energy independence, all while aligning with Tarquin Soll's autarky strategy."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""That's the essence of opportunity...."
entries.dialogueText: "That's the essence of opportunity. What matters is that you seize it when it appears. And remember, it's not just about taking that leap, but about what you do once you've landed."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "He took a sip of coffee. His face a..."
entries.dialogueText: He took a sip of coffee. His face assumed a contemplative expression.

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso

entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""I would argue that the transient n..."
entries.dialogueText: "I would argue that the transient nature of reputation is what makes it important. It's the soil in which the seed of legacy grows."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""A noble perspective. But isn't it..."
entries.dialogueText: "A noble perspective. But isn't it through our reputation and legacy that our integrity and service are ultimately judged?"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Your past actions show nothing but..."
entries.dialogueText: "Your past actions show nothing but a ruthless pursuit of profit, at the expense of the people and environment. That's hardly a reputation or a legacy to be proud of."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""A harsh critique, but not an unexp..."
entries.dialogueText: "A harsh critique, but not an unexpected one. I see profit as a means to a greater end. It enables us to drive progress, change lives."

entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""As for my legacy, it will be for h..."
entries.dialogueText: "As for my legacy, it will be for history to judge, not you or me."

entries.dialogueText: "It seems we are at a crossroads with Gasom. The numbers tell a tale of struggle and potential."

entries.dialogueText: "My old friend Ewald reached out to me for assistance. Out of respect for our shared history -- and my small stake in the company -- I couldn't refuse."

entries.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
entries.title: Ewald Alphonso: ""Thanks to Gus' Rizian connections,..."
entries.dialogueText: "Thanks to Gus' Rizian connections, investors from the kingdom are now interested in Gasom, a development that could steer us clear of the looming crisis."

entries.title: Player: ""I'm intrigued by the untapped fiel..."
entries.dialogueText: "I'm intrigued by the untapped fields. What's the potential return if we invest in these new areas?"

entries.title: Player: ""Will the investment help keep Gaso..."
entries.dialogueText: "Will the investment help keep Gasom from having to downsize its operations?"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""That's a risk, Mr. Alphonso. What..."
entries.dialogueText: "That's a risk, Mr. Alphonso. What if the investment doesn't pay off as expected?"

entries.dialogueText: "It was only when his father fell ill that he took over and transformed the farm. He took risks, made some mistakes, but ultimately, he tripled their output in just a few years."

entries.speaker: Gus Manger

entries.dialogueText: “Your concerns, Mr. President, remind me of a time when I was working with OMEC. We were bringing in foreign investments to revitalize the local companies. There were protests, people who were scared of change, who thought we were selling out. But we weathered the backlash, stood by our decisions.”

entries.dialogueText: "A truly inspiring story, Gus. This is the kind of innovation and growth we should be fostering in Sordland."
